title: Human Evolution
seo_title: Grade 12 Life Sciences: Human Evolution Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Similarities and differences between humans and African apes (bipedalism, the foramen magnum, the pelvis, the spine, brain size, teeth and jaws); the fossil evidence for human evolution in South Africa (Taung Child, Mrs Ples, Little Foot, Australopithecus sediba, Homo naledi); the Out of Africa hypothesis; genetic evidence from mitochondrial DNA. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 12, Life Sciences: Human evolution)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): humans and African apes, bipedalism, South African hominid fossils, Out of Africa and mitochondrial DNA. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Bipedalism is a key feature of hominids.
key_sub: Modern humans first evolved in Africa.
body_html:
How to think about it

Humans share many features with other primates: forward-facing eyes, opposable thumbs and nails instead of claws. Humans differ from African apes in being bipedal: the foramen magnum is under the skull, the spine is S-shaped and the pelvis is short and wide. Humans have a larger brain, a flatter face, smaller jaws and smaller canine teeth.

South Africa's Cradle of Humankind has many hominid fossils: Mrs Ples and Little Foot at Sterkfontein, Australopithecus sediba at Malapa and Homo naledi in the Rising Star Cave; the Taung Child comes from the North West. The Out of Africa hypothesis says that Homo sapiens evolved in Africa and spread across the world; mitochondrial DNA, inherited from the mother, supports it.

Example

Where is the foramen magnum in a bipedal hominid?

The spine enters from below.

Answer: under the skull, towards the front

Example

Which species is the Taung Child?

Described by Raymond Dart

Answer: Australopithecus africanus

Common mistakes

  • Thinking humans evolved from modern chimpanzees.
  • Thinking a bigger brain came before bipedalism.
  • Thinking all hominid fossils come from Europe.

faq.q: Why is the Cradle of Humankind a World Heritage Site?
faq.a: It has one of the richest collections of hominid fossils in the world.

faq.q: Why is mitochondrial DNA useful for tracing ancestry?
faq.a: It is passed only from mother to child and changes slowly, so it can be traced back many generations.

items.q: What does the Hardy–Weinberg principle state?
c: allele frequencies stay constant in a population if no evolutionary forces act
items.e: p² + 2pq + q² = 1.

items.e: It supported Oparin and Haldane's idea.
